Consult Summary:
- Telemedicine consult for worsening, widespread itchy, sore, red, dry rash consistent with eczema flare; plan for stronger topical steroid and antihistamine; continue emollients; follow-up in 2 weeks or earlier if worsening.

History:
- Presenting complaint: 3–4 days of worsening sore, red, very itchy, dry skin rash.
- Distribution: Chest, hands, arms; worst in antecubital fossae (inside elbows); generalized dryness/itchiness.
- Associated features: Cracked areas; denies weeping; no noted scratch marks; patient does not think skin is thickened.
- Pertinent negatives: None clearly confirmed for fever or joint pain (physician asked; patient did not directly confirm).
- Past medical history: Eczema; asthma. Family history: Mother with migraine and thyroid disease (patient said hypothyroidism; clinician repeated hyperthyroidism—conflict noted).
- Medications prior to visit:
  - Diprobase emollient cream (dose/route/frequency not documented) — used regularly.
  - “Dermal” shower product/soap substitute (dose/route/frequency not documented) — used regularly.
  - Hydrocortisone OTC topical steroid previously tried; patient reports it did not help (current use unclear; dose/route/frequency not documented).
  - Asthma: “Blue inhaler” used as needed (name/dose/frequency not documented).
  - No current antihistamines; prior OTC antihistamine (likely cetirizine) tried without benefit.
- Allergies: No known drug allergies.
- Social history and preventive care: Not discussed.

Examination:
- Vitals: Not documented.
- Exam findings: None performed (telemedicine). Patient-reported skin findings as above; no weeping; cracked areas; no visible scratch marks reported; patient does not think skin is thickened.

Impression:
- Widespread eczema (atopic dermatitis) flare, worsening over several days.

Plan:
- Medications:
  - Fexofenadine (antihistamine) prescribed; dose/route/frequency not documented.
  - Betnovate (topical steroid) prescribed: apply a thin layer in small amounts (fingertip unit guidance discussed) to affected areas twice daily for “the next couple of weeks.”
- Skin care:
  - Continue emollients and soap substitute: continue “Dermal” product in shower and emollient cream (patient reported Diprobase; clinician later said “diprovate”—see conflict).
- Safety/monitoring:
  - If no improvement after 2 weeks or if worsening sooner, contact clinic.
  - Stop and seek care if any adverse reaction occurs.
- Prescription:
  - E-prescription sent to Boots pharmacy for collection.
- Follow-up:
  - Reassess if symptoms not improving within ~2 weeks or earlier if deteriorating.

Quality checks:
● Missing expected elements:
  - Clarification of fever/joint pain review of systems.
  - Detailed medication list with doses/routes/frequencies (fexofenadine, hydrocortisone, emollients, “blue inhaler”).
  - Triggers/exposures, infection signs beyond weeping, impact on sleep/activities, and smoking status not discussed.
  - No physical exam or vitals.
● Internal conflicts:
  - Family history: Patient stated mother has hypothyroidism; clinician restated as hyperthyroidism (conflict noted).
  - Emollient name: Patient said Diprobase; clinician later said “diprovate” (likely misspeak; conflict noted).
  - Current hydrocortisone use unclear: patient reports trying it without benefit; unclear if still using.
● Transcript quality:
  - Some unclear/inaudible segments and brand-name pronunciations; overall history and plan understandable.
